data_directory.name: Data directory
data_directory.description: Where login cookies, webhooks and proxies are stored. Keep /config/zalo_bot unless you have a reason to change it — changing it loses the Zalo session and you must scan the QR code again.

session_secret.name: Session signing key
session_secret.description: Can be left EMPTY: the add-on generates a key unique to this machine and keeps it, so logins survive restarts. Fill this in only if you want to manage the key yourself. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

admin_password.name: Admin password
admin_password.description: Can be left EMPTY: the add-on generates a random password, writes it to THONG-TIN-DANG-NHAP.txt in the data directory (open it with the File editor or Samba) and prints it to the Log tab on every start. Fill this in to choose your own.

api_key.name: Send API key
api_key.description: Can be left EMPTY: the add-on generates a key, keeps it, and writes it to THONG-TIN-DANG-NHAP.txt in the data directory alongside the admin password. You only need this key when calling the sending APIs directly from a REST command or script — the HACS integration does not need it, it logs in with the account.

github_token.name: GitHub token
github_token.description: REQUIRED for the first run. Read-only GitHub token for the zalo_bot repo (issued by the repo owner): GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Fine-grained tokens, pick only the zalo_bot repo, permission Contents = Read-only. After the first run an expired token does NOT stop the add-on: it keeps running the saved code and just cannot update; paste a new token and restart to update.

app_version.name: Code version
app_version.description: Empty = the version shipped with the add-on. Enter a tag (e.g. v2026.11.19.1) to pin one, or latest for the newest release (needs a valid token).
